findings.problem: `quotient` repeats the whole proof of `of_surjective` (lines 82–89). Both obtain the exponent `n`, take a preimage of `y` under a surjection, and push `hn` through the linear map with `congrArg f` and `map_smul`/`map_zero`. The only change is that `f` is `N.mkQ`. `of_surjective` is declared earlier in the same file and needs only `CommSemiring`, `AddCommMonoid` and `Module`, so it already covers the `CommRing`/`AddCommGroup` quotient setting. A fix to one proof would have to be copied into the other.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove the quotient case from the general lemma:

theorem IsKilledByIdealPower.quotient {I : Ideal R} (h : IsKilledByIdealPower R M I)
    (N : Submodule R M) : IsKilledByIdealPower R (M ⧸ N) I :=
  h.of_surjective N.mkQ N.mkQ_surjective

Hypotheses: the target module has type `M ⧸ N : Type v`, which fits `{N : Type w}` for any universe. The instances `AddCommMonoid (M ⧸ N)` and `Module R (M ⧸ N)` come from `AddCommGroup M`, which gives an `AddCommMonoid`. The lemma `of_surjective` is in the `AddCommMonoid` section with `variable {R M}` implicit, so `h.of_surjective` elaborates. The statement of `of_surjective` does not change.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated nontrivial argument (preimage, push the annihilation identity through a linear map). Surjectivity-transfer is then proved once. The quotient lemma becomes a one-line corollary whose reason is visible.
